title: Add B200 tuned hardware profile (experimental) behind feature flag + compatibility checks
author: Isabella Rossi
release_notes: Adds an experimental B200 hardware tuning profile gated behind `runtime.hardware_profiles.experimental_b200`. Includes explicit CUDA/driver/runtime compatibility checks and safe fallback to H100/default presets when incompatible or when detection is ambiguous.
description: Summary: This PR introduces an initial B200 tuned profile into the hardware tuning profile pack, but keeps it disabled by default behind a dedicated feature flag. The loader will only select the B200 profile when (a) the node GPU SKU normalizes to a known B200 identifier, (b) the experimental flag is enabled, and (c) the runtime + CUDA + driver versions satisfy a minimum compatibility window. If any of those checks fail (or we cannot determine versions reliably), we fall back to the existing default selection logic (H100 preset where appropriate, otherwise baseline). Motivation: Early B200 capacity is limited and heterogeneous. We want to unblock bring-up / perf validation without creating an accidental fleet-wide behavior change or a support burden for Dedicated/Private operators. The goal is to make “enable B200 profile” a deliberate action with strong guardrails and clear logs. Non-goals: This does not add new kernels from scratch, does not change public API behavior, and does not make B200 the default anywhere. Key changes: 1) Profile pack: Adds `b200.experimental.v0` profile with conservative defaults for scheduler/batching and KV-cache budgeting. 2) Feature flag: Adds `runtime.hardware_profiles.experimental_b200` (default false). 3) Compatibility checks: Introduces a small compatibility gate that requires minimum CUDA runtime version + minimum NVIDIA driver version + a minimum runtime build capability; the check is logged at startup and exposed in `effective_config` output. 4) Selection logic: Loader only selects B200 profile if all checks pass; otherwise it logs a structured reason and selects the next best profile. 5) Observability: Emits `runtime_profile_selected{profile=...,source=...}` and `runtime_profile_incompatible_reason` for quick triage during canaries. Operator notes: For Hosted/Dedicated, do not enable the flag at fleet level until perf-canary + pool canaries are green. For Private, enabling the flag without meeting minimum versions will not fail startup; it will fallback and log the reason. Compatibility assumptions (initial): B200 requires a newer driver/CUDA stack than H100. The exact minimums are encoded in `compat/b200_min_versions` and documented in the startup log line `hardware_profile_compatibility`. If we can’t parse driver/CUDA versions from the environment, we consider the system incompatible and do not select the B200 profile. Rollout plan: Land behind flag; enable in perf-canary runners first; enable for a single internal B200 pool in us-east; expand by region only after 48h stability (p95 latency + error rate + OOM rate) meets the thresholds in the rollout runbook. Testing: Unit tests for version parsing + gate logic; integration tests for override precedence still passing; CI adds a small loader test fixture for ambiguous SKU strings (should NOT select B200).
commits: profile-pack: add b200 experimental profile skeleton + defaults
runtime: add `experimental_b200` feature flag + config plumbing
runtime: implement B200 compatibility gate (driver/CUDA/runtime) and fallback reasons
observability: add metrics + startup log for profile compatibility matrix
tests: add unit tests for version parsing and selection behavior
changed_areas: runtime/compat (driver/CUDA minimums for B200, parsing helpers)
notable_snippets: Selection gate (simplified): if sku==B200 && flag.experimental_b200 && compat_ok() => select b200.experimental.v0 else fallback();
Startup log: hardware_profile_compatibility gpu_sku=B200 runtime=1.34.0 cuda=12.4 driver=550.54.15 b200_compat=true reason=""
review_conversation: Hiro Tanaka: Can we ensure this cannot be selected accidentally on H100 nodes where the provider reports a weird name? I’ve seen “NVIDIA B200 SXM” and “NVIDIA B200” but also truncated strings. Please make sure the normalization list is strict and we log what we matched.

Isabella Rossi (author): Updated normalization to require an explicit B200 token match and added a structured log field `gpu_sku_raw` + `gpu_sku_normalized`. Also added a test case for truncated strings that should NOT match.

Sofia Ivanova: Scheduler defaults look aggressive for early bring-up (queue limits + decode fairness). I’d rather keep them close to balanced until we have tail latency curves. Can we start conservative and adjust later?

Isabella Rossi (author): Agreed. I pulled back `max_inflight_requests` and set decode fairness to the same baseline as H100 balanced; kept the batch cap modest. Marked the profile description with “conservative first pass; tune in follow-up PR after canary curves.”
Ethan Park: Please add explicit version checks (not just a comment). Also, the behavior on unknown versions should be “do not enable” not “assume OK.”
Isabella Rossi (author): Done. Compatibility gate now fails closed: unknown/parse failure => incompatible => fallback. Added unit tests for parse failures.
Quentin Harris: Can we document the compatibility window in the logs in a way Support can copy/paste? Something like `required_driver>=X required_cuda>=Y`.
Isabella Rossi (author): Added `required_*` fields to the startup log line and included them in `effective-config` output to reduce back-and-forth for Private deployments.
Irene Choi: Please keep rollout friction low: we should be able to flip this per pool. Does the flag support per-deployment override, not just global?

Isabella Rossi (author): Yes; it’s a normal config flag and participates in the existing override order (fleet default < pool < deployment). Added a short note in the config docstring and validated with the override precedence integration test.
Sean Gallagher (SRE): What’s the operational blast radius if the B200 profile triggers OOMs? We need a single toggle to disable without redeploying.

Isabella Rossi (author): Disabling the feature flag immediately prevents selection on new processes; for running pods you’ll still need a restart, but SRE can flip the pool config and restart via the standard rolling restart. Also, fallback selection is automatic when the gate fails; included incompatibility metrics to confirm.
Hiro Tanaka: OK with the conservative first pass behind flag. Please link follow-up ticket to tune kernels when we get more B200 time.
Isabella Rossi (author): Added follow-up note to ENG-4826 and referenced the perf-canary plan in the PR description.
post_merge_notes: Follow-ups: (1) add B200 workload matrix coverage in benchmark-lab runner once more B200 runners are available, (2) revisit scheduler fairness + batch caps after first canary curves, (3) confirm Private docs mention fail-closed compatibility behavior.
